headline: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon takes the top benchmark spot but stays gated; Alphabet holds capex near $200B; a Claude Code extension is…

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's twelve minutes to three UTC on Saturday, October thirty-first. This is ARA Radio. Google has a new top-ranked model, but few can use it yet.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That's Gemini 4 Carbon, announced on Alphabet's earnings call. Google said it was excited to be leading at the frontier.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Relays put it first on the new Artificial Analysis index, fifty-nine against fifty-eight for Claude Opus five point five. Mercor's agent benchmark also has it first, at eighty-four point two percent on a single attempt.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Access is limited to cyber defenders for now. There's no general release date, no pricing and no independent testing yet.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: On that same call, Alphabet kept its capital spending guidance for the year at one hundred ninety-five to two hundred five billion dollars. Free cash flow was negative nine point one billion in the third quarter.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The company also said it began renting third-party computing capacity at the end of the quarter, which it expects to squeeze cloud margins. Cloud revenue still jumped one hundred three percent, to thirty point seven billion dollars.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That sits against Thursday's chip rout, when Intel fell nearly thirty percent. The next test is Monday.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: On security, Anthropic says someone used Cursor's extension marketplace to publish a tampered copy of the Claude Code extension. Anthropic says its own systems were not compromised and only Cursor users are affected.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Relays say the fake versions planted an attacker key. That detail is not confirmed, and we have no statement from Cursor yet.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: On funding, hosts on the 20VC podcast talked about Anthropic issuing about one hundred billion dollars of stock after its filing. They also said Meta announced a raise of up to ninety-five billion dollars.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Sources disagree on Anthropic's first-half revenue, so treat that figure with care until the listing documents are parsed.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: One more thread. OpenAI claims its models disproved a major computer science conjecture. The outside reviewers wrote an open letter saying their involvement is not certification, so there's no verdict.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: To watch: a release date for Carbon, a Cursor post-mortem, Anthropic's pricing and listing date, and Monday's chip trading.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That's ARA Radio. We'll be back when the picture changes.
